skill.name: sharepoint-audit
skill.description: Guide local SharePoint Online permission audits using PowerShell, Python, certificate authentication, and generated Markdown or HTML reports.
skill.summary: Run local SharePoint Online permission audits and produce sensitive-access reports.
skill.author: Aqualia

security_audit.summary: The skill is a legitimate SharePoint audit workflow, but it instructs the assistant to run local PowerShell and Python commands. Several static hits are inline code formatting rather than execution, while the command and module-install steps remain real operational risks that require user authorization.

remediation.issue: The skill runs local PowerShell and Python commands that can affect Microsoft 365 audit workflows.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before running each command, and show the exact command with arguments before execution.

remediation.issue: The module installation step may fetch dependencies from external sources.
remediation.suggestion: Document trusted module sources, expected module names, and version pinning for PnP.PowerShell dependencies.

remediation.issue: Generated reports may contain sensitive SharePoint permission data.
remediation.suggestion: Keep the existing warning and add guidance to store reports in a restricted local directory.

content.value_statement: SharePoint permission reviews are difficult when data spans sites and requires certificate authentication. This skill guides a local audit and produces readable reports for review.
actual_capabilities: Collects tenant ID, client ID, certificate path, internal domains, and site targets before running the audit.
Checks that PowerShell 7.4+, Python 3.10+, and PnP.PowerShell are available locally.
Runs a PowerShell module installer for the SharePoint audit agent workflow.
Runs the Python audit agent with a site URL or CSV input and an output directory.
Points users to generated Markdown or HTML reports after a successful run.
Reminds users that generated reports contain sensitive permission data.
limitations: Requires local PowerShell, Python, and Microsoft 365 audit dependencies.
Requires valid certificate-based authentication and a configured PFX password environment variable.
Does not audit SharePoint without local command execution.
Generated reports must be protected because they may contain sensitive access data.

use_cases.title: Review one site before a permission cleanup
use_cases.description: Audit a single SharePoint Online site and inspect the generated report before changing access.

use_cases.title: Run batch audits from a CSV list
use_cases.description: Use a CSV-defined site list to collect reports across multiple SharePoint locations.

use_cases.title: Prepare evidence for access governance
use_cases.description: Generate local permission reports that support an internal access review process.

prompt_templates.title: Audit one SharePoint site
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me audit one SharePoint Online site. Ask me for the tenant ID, client ID, PFX path, internal domains, site URL, and PFX_PASS confirmation before running anything.

prompt_templates.title: Check prerequisites first
prompt_templates.prompt: Before running the SharePoint audit, confirm that PowerShell 7.4+, Python 3.10+, and PnP.PowerShell are available locally.

prompt_templates.title: Run a CSV batch audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through a SharePoint audit using a CSV of site URLs. Confirm every local command before execution and write output under ./runs.

prompt_templates.title: Review audit output safely
prompt_templates.prompt: After the SharePoint audit completes, show me where the HTML report is located and remind me how to handle sensitive permission data.

output_examples.input: Audit this SharePoint site with certificate authentication.
output_examples.output: The assistant asks for the tenant ID, client ID, certificate path, internal domains, target site URL, and PFX_PASS confirmation before proposing commands.

output_examples.input: Run the batch audit from my CSV file.
output_examples.output: The assistant confirms the CSV path, prepares the local Python audit command, and asks for approval before execution.
The assistant points to the generated report path and warns that the file may contain sensitive SharePoint permission details.

best_practices: Review every local command before approving execution.
Use Sites.Selected read permission unless write permission is explicitly required.
Store generated reports in a restricted location and delete them when no longer needed.
anti_patterns: Do not paste certificate passwords into chat or command output.
Do not run module installation commands in an untrusted environment.
Do not grant write permission unless the audit process truly needs it.

faq.question: Does this skill run commands on my machine?
faq.answer: Yes. It guides local PowerShell and Python commands, so you should review and approve each command.

faq.question: What credentials does it need?
faq.answer: It needs tenant and app identifiers, a PFX certificate path, and confirmation that PFX_PASS is set.

faq.question: Can it audit multiple sites?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill supports a site URL or a CSV-defined batch of SharePoint sites.

faq.question: Does it send audit data to a cloud service?
faq.answer: The skill text says to use local commands only, except for module installation. Review dependencies before running.

faq.question: Are the generated reports sensitive?
faq.answer: Yes. Reports can include permission and access data, so store them with restricted access.

faq.question: Should I use read or write Sites.Selected permission?
faq.answer: Use read by default. Only use write permission when you explicitly authorize and require it.
